Liz W.: Hey team - POC with AcmeCorp is hitting errors when using our TS + Python SDKs behind their corporate proxy. They need this for tomorrow's exec demo. Any quick fixes?
Alex K.: What error are they seeing? 429s or connection timeouts?
Liz W.: Mostly timeouts and occasional 502s from the gateway. Also they reported a 401 once but couldn't repro it.
Maria V.: Can you grab a request id or last 6 chars of request-id from the error? That helps trace on our side.
Liz W.: Sent logs from their infra: "request_id=ab12c3" and an excerpt: 
```
Error: connect ETIMEDOUT 10.10.0.1:443
at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (net.js:1191:14)
```:
Sam R.: ETIMEDOUT behind corp proxies usually means SDK not using proxy env or TLS interception causing handshake drop. Ask them to try setting HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY in their environment first.
Liz W.: I've asked them to set those. Any SDK-level opts?
Sam R.: Yes. For Python our client honors env vars, but if they're using requests directly, show them this snippet to enable retries + proxies:
```python
import os
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from requests.packages.urllib3.util.retry import Retry
import requests

os.environ['HTTP_PROXY'] = 'http://proxy.corp:8080'
os.environ['HTTPS_PROXY'] = 'http://proxy.corp:8080'

s = requests.Session()
retries = Retry(total=5, backoff_factor=0.5, status_forcelist=[429,502,503,504])
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))
resp = s.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json=payload, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'}, timeout=60)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```
Maria V.: For the TS SDK (node) they should configure proxy and timeouts:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, timeoutMs: 60000, maxRetries: 4 })
// or if using axios directly
const axios = require('axios');
const instance = axios.create({ timeout: 60000, proxy: { host: 'proxy.corp', port: 8080 } })
```
Alex K.: Also check they aren't hitting org rate limits. If they see many 429s include headers: x-rate-limit-limit, x-rate-limit-remaining, x-rate-limit-reset. Ask them to paste those.
Liz W.: They pasted this header block: 
```
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1718205600
```
Liz W.: So looks like they exhausted a low quota during stress tests. Pricing/legal asked if Dedicated reserve would avoid that - can we confirm?
Maria V.: Dedicated + Reserved capacity removes shared rate throttles. Liz, flag this to the deal: if they need predictable throughput for the demo, recommend short Dedicated eval or increase hosted quota for trial accounts. I'll follow up with pricing numbers.
Sam R.: For the 502s we saw a gateway trace: "upstream_reset by peer" and the request_id ab12c3. I've pulled the runtime logs and see intermittent backend OOMs on model shard -> fallback triggered. InfraBot, any spikes on the GPU pool?
InfraBot: GPU pool shard-5 had a brief OOM spike at 2024-06-12T18:02:00Z, fallback served smaller variant for ~45s, ~12 requests affected.
Sam R.: That matches their timestamps. Short-term: advise the customer to set client retries (status_forcelist includes 502) and exponential backoff. We should also prod eng-runtime to raise shard threshold or enable auto-burst for dedicated eval.
Liz W.: Action items for us: 1) Share the Python/TS snippets with Acme. 2) Offer a temporary hosted quota bump for demo window. 3) Ask infra to scope a quick Dedicated eval if they want predictable SLOs. 4) Get security questionnaire answers RACI.
Alex K.: I'll open a quick ticket to eng-runtime and tag @oncall for ETA on OOM mitigation. Ticket id: RW-7832. Sam, can you attach the runtime logs to it?
Sam R.: Attached. Also added suggested client config snippets and proxy troubleshooting notes.
Maria V.: Liz — for the security questionnaire they wanted details on data residency and KMS. I'll draft answers tonight and drop in the Deal folder.
Liz W.: Perfect. Acme also asked about SDK behavior when the private deployment (VPC) is used — they need confirmation that proxies are allowed and TLS termination remains client-side. Sam?
Sam R.: For Private (VPC) deployments customers control network egress. Our SDKs work the same; proxy envs still effective. TLS stays end-to-end unless their proxy does TLS interception. If they need HSM/KMS details, Maria will add that.
Liz W.: Great — will relay.
Alex K.: Follow-ups: ask Acme to run a small reproducible script that hits generate 10x with 1s delay so we can repro locally behind a proxy. If they can't, ask for a HAR or tcpdump capture.
Liz W.: Sending that now. Thanks all — will update thread with their test results. :thumbsup:
